purpose: Machine-readable provenance and comparison contract for a Rust-first reproduction of the published seven-task HDC/VSA classification benchmark. This manifest records source and protocol review state; it does not attest that datasets were downloaded, licensed for redistribution, or evaluated.

reference_protocol.paper_title: Classification using hyperdimensional computing: a review with comparative analysis
reference_protocol.reference_defaults: Keep paper-default configurations in a distinct track. Do not claim exact reproduction until the benchmark code revision, transforms, weights and split handling are pinned for every task.

policies.data_handling: Download only from recorded upstream or author-designated sources. This repository does not redistribute raw data or derived benchmark artifacts.
policies.license_handling: License claims transcribe upstream metadata where available; they are not legal advice or a determination that redistribution/transformation is permitted.
policies.artifact_hashing: A source artifact is not trusted until its bytes, SHA-256, source URL and deterministic transformed-split digest are recorded.
policies.preprocessing: Fit scalers, vocabularies, feature selection and learned transforms on training data only, unless the cited reference protocol explicitly specifies otherwise.
policies.evaluation: Use published test splits when available; do not tune on test data; report per-task outcomes before aggregate summaries.
policies.fairness: Compare reference-default configurations separately from equal-budget tuning. Methods share the exact same splits and query samples.
policies.claim_ceiling: Metadata validation is not data ingestion, license clearance, benchmark execution, or a SOTA claim.

sources.citation: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images.

reference_preprocessing.notes: The reference suite uses features extracted by a pretrained two-layer CNN, not raw RGB pixels. Pin extractor source revision, weights digest, output layer, normalization and transformed-feature SHA-256.

split_policy.notes: Audit the reference code for exact split, ordering and transform. Any raw-pixel experiment is a separate track.

sources.citation: Krilova et al. (2018). EMG Data for Gestures. UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI 10.24432/C5ZP5C.

reference_preprocessing.notes: Eight forearm EMG channels and multiple subjects. Pin segmentation/statistics and handling of rest/unmarked class 0; random row splits risk subject and temporal leakage.

split_policy.notes: Pin the reference split; report subject-held-out generalization separately.

sources.citation: Koehn (2005). Europarl: A Parallel Corpus for Statistical Machine Translation.

reference_preprocessing.notes: Training uses Wortschatz text and testing uses Europarl. Pin corpus versions, language subset, normalization, trigram vocabulary policy and scaling. Fit learned vocabulary on training text only.

split_policy.notes: Distinct train/test corpus sources are intentional; do not replace this with a random split.

sources.citation: Cole & Fanty (1991). ISOLET. UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI 10.24432/C51G69.

reference_preprocessing.notes: UCI reports 7,797 examples and a speaker-grouped split. Preserve isolet1+2+3+4 for training and isolet5 for testing; do not repartition rows randomly.

split_policy.notes: Record source file names and dropped/missing observations.

sources.citation: LeCun, Cortes & Burges (2010). MNIST handwritten digit database.

reference_preprocessing.notes: Reference suite uses features from a pretrained two-layer CNN, not directly the raw pixels. Pin architecture/source revision, weights digest, output layer, normalization and transformed-feature digest; raw-pixel results are separate.

split_policy.notes: Keep the canonical 60,000 training / 10,000 test partition.

sources.citation: Reiss (2012). PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring. UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI 10.24432/C5NW2H.

reference_preprocessing.notes: Preserve subject/session structure, missing-value handling and timestamps. Do not randomly split overlapping windows across train/test.

split_policy.notes: Pin reference preprocessing/splits; report subject-held-out performance separately.

datasets.display_name: UCI Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones

sources.citation: Reyes-Ortiz et al. (2013). Human Activity Recognition Using Smartphones. UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI 10.24432/C54S4K.

reference_preprocessing.notes: Preserve packaged train/test windows and subject identifiers. For end-to-end raw IMU work, report windowing/filtering as a separate track.

split_policy.notes: Preserve the packaged subject-disjoint split; audit the feature-generation procedure before describing results as raw-sensor end-to-end.
